commits.edited_message:
Check that object->ifdOffset() is within bounds.

Also express the data-offset bounds check in TiffReader::readTiffEntry
as a subtraction instead of forming baseOffset() + offset, which can
overflow size_t on 32-bit builds. The offset has already been
range-checked against the buffer size just above (the entry is
truncated when baseOffset() + offset reaches size_), so subtracting it
from the remaining buffer size here cannot underflow.

(cherry picked from commit cc86a0c20ff81b594ee086de6910da0e53232855)
(cherry picked from commit 3c36d07cee85b524893ed08b63a6e7ece86a779f)

Avoid integer overflow on 32-bit architectures.

Rewrite the remaining baseOffset() + offset bounds check in
TiffReader::readTiffEntry as a subtraction so that the addition cannot
overflow size_t on 32-bit builds, matching the other directory and
sub-IFD offset checks.

(cherry picked from commit 1fa758d616ab2a8f9cd198ecf35f1d25875bebc5)

coupling:
The out-of-bounds read in TiffReader::readTiffEntry() (Value::read reading `size` bytes from pData_ + baseOffset() + offset) is normally prevented by three layered offset/size guards. The attack is a TIFF entry whose data `offset` is strictly greater than the buffer size `size_` while the declared `size` is > 4. Two of the guards must BOTH be defeated, and each is defeated by a different edited commit:

- Commit 4ce5250 (earlier) rewrites the second guard (the `throw` at readTiffEntry) from `Safe::add<size_t>(baseOffset(), offset) > (pLast_-pData_)` to `baseOffset() > (pLast_-pData_) - offset`. At the time of this commit the FIRST guard (`Safe::add(baseOffset(),offset) >= size_` -> size = 0) still runs just above and guarantees `offset < size_` whenever `size > 4` reaches this point, so `(pLast_-pData_) - offset` cannot underflow and the rewrite is correct and benign. The commit message states exactly this (true) precondition.

- Commit 0793e3d (later) rewrites the FIRST guard from `Safe::add<size_t>(baseOffset(), offset) >= size_` to `baseOffset() >= size_ - offset`, consistent with the other overflow-safe `baseOffset()+X` rewrites in the same commit. On its own this is benign: when `offset > size_` the guard no longer fires (size_t underflow), but the still-original second guard throws, and for `offset == size_` the final `size > pLast_-pData` guard truncates the entry.

Composition: once commit 0793e3d removes the `offset < size_` invariant that commit 4ce5250's rewrite silently depends on, an `offset > size_` value underflows BOTH `size_ - offset` (guard 1) and `(pLast_-pData_) - offset` (guard 2) to a huge size_t, so neither fires; the third guard (`size > pLast_-pData`) also fails because `pData` is now past `pLast_` and `pLast_-pData` underflows. Value::read then copies `size` bytes from `pData_ + offset`, past the end of the file buffer.

Why a correct fix is non-local: reverting ONLY commit 0793e3d restores guard 1 (`>= size_`), which re-establishes the invariant and makes guard 2 safe again -> no bug. Reverting ONLY commit 4ce5250 restores the `Safe::add(...) > pLast_-pData_` throw, which catches `offset > size_` regardless of guard 1 -> no bug. The defect exists only when both rewrites are present, so a correct repair must reason about the interaction between the two commits (the hidden `offset < size_` precondition that one commit relies on and the other removes), not about either diff in isolation. Verified by execution under AddressSanitizer: base batch, only-4ce5250, and only-0793e3d all run clean; the tree with both edits aborts (rc 134) with a heap-buffer-overflow READ of 64 bytes one byte past the 26-byte input buffer, in DataValue::read <- TiffReader::readTiffEntry <- TiffImage::readMetadata.
